mechanism_narrative: A 2% quarterly increase in GDP (GDPC1) indicates strengthening economic growth, leading to increased consumer spending and, subsequently, higher S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 50% of quarters with 2%+ GDPC1 growth.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 1.5%, signaling a tightening monetary cycle, S&P 500 forward returns tend to decline over the next 20 trading days due to increased borrowing costs.
failure_condition: 20-day forward SPX returns remain positive in > 70% of periods with FEDFUNDS above 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Jointly, when UNRATE falls below 6% and PAYEMS increases by 200,000+ in a month, signaling a strong labor market, S&P 500 returns tend to increase over the next 5 trading days due to heightened consumer confidence.
failure_condition: 5-day forward SPX returns are negative in > 40% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A 1.5% monthly increase in INDPRO, indicating a surge in industrial production, predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to increased economic activity.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC for this mechanism remains below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) increases by 1%+ in a month, signaling increased consumer spending, and concurrently HOUST (housing starts) rises by 5%+, indicating a strong housing market, S&P 500 returns tend to increase over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward SPX returns are negative in > 30% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL (inflation rate) exceeding 3% for two consecutive months signals impending monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward SPX returns remain positive in > 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: Always, the direction of PAYEMS (non-farm payroll employment) changes predicts the direction of S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days, as labor market health directly influences consumer spending and economic growth.
failure_condition: 5-day forward SPX return direction mismatches PAYEMS direction change in > 45% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-shock recovery regime, a 0.5% increase in GDPC1 (GDP) within a quarter, coupled with a 2% increase in HOUST (housing starts), predicts a stronger recovery, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward SPX returns are negative in > 40% of triggered post-shock recovery instances.
